podcast.body: An anthemic 1981 duet with David Bowie, widely considered a masterpiece for both artists. It reached number one in the UK and number 28 on the US Hot 100, getting Bowie back into the Top 40 after six years. The song features explosive vocals by Freddie Mercury and an "immortal" bassline by John Deacon, which was later stolen by Vanilla Ice for "Ice Ice Baby." Primarily written by Bowie, it is a song of protest, fellowship, and love. "With explosive vocals by Freddie Mercury and Immortal Baseline by Queen's Inventive Basis John Deacon, one that rapper Vanilla Ice would later steal for Ice Ice Baby, and lyrics primarily written by Bowie."

podcast.body: The dramatic 1981 duet between British rock legends Queen and David Bowie, which peaked in the US at a modest number 29 in early 1982. Its iconic baseline was famously sampled and became the foundation for Vanilla Ice's 1990 number one hit "Ice Ice Baby."
